properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 21 at 2:37PM MDT until October 21 at 3:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 237 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles south of
Zuni Pueblo, moving northeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Zuni Pueblo, Black Rock and Chi Chil Tah.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 1:04PM MDT until October 21 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 104 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across Zion Canyon within Zion National Park. Up to 0.25
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to
0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of slot canyons and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Zion National Park.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 21 at 12:35PM MDT until October 22 at 12:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is imminent
or occurring. Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall
will continue trough at least Thursday morning. This coupled with
near-saturated soils will allow rapidly increasing flows across all
waterways within the warned area, including all of the Glen Canyon
National Recreation Area. Increasingly high flows are expected in,
but not limited to...the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek,
Last Chance Creek, Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and
tributaries. Many backcountry roads within this area are expected
to become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1208 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges continue
to indicate heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the warned area. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches are possible in
the warned area through Thursday morning.
- Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, including the Escalante
region. Kodachrome State Park, Tropic, Cannonville, Escalante,
and Big Water
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks can become unstable and
unsafe.
properties.area: Garfield, UT; Kane, UT; San Juan, UT

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 11:02AM MST until October 21 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Moenkopi Wash in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 300 PM MST /400 PM MDT/.

* At 1102 AM MST /1202 PM MDT/, a river gauge on the Moenkopi Wash
reported a rapid rise of around 8 feet from thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Moenkopi Wash. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Moenkopi Wash.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Moenkopi Wash.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 160 between mile markers 318 and 321. U.S. Highway 89 between
mile markers 476 and 478. State Route 264 between mile markers 323
and 324.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River, Begashibito Wash, Fivemile Wash, Moenkopi
Wash and Hamblin Wash.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Moenkopi Wash. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:34AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end of this
week. There is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage
next week after northeasterly winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 945 PM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 21 at 8:32AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...

Satilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 845 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Satilla River at Atkinson.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Warners Landing, Louis Landing and
secondary roads around KOA campgrounds begin to flood. At 14.0
feet, River Rock Road begins to experience flooding across the
road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 14.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 13.5 feet Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
